title: Build a five-minute plan for an evidence-led recycling trial
instructions: Plan a response about using a fair-comparison method learned in science to improve a school recycling point. The five-minute routine is practice guidance.

parts.prompt: Which planning sequence is most efficient?

options.text: Decode requirements, choose one focus, map introduction/body/conclusion, then audit
Write the conclusion first, then invent evidence
List vocabulary for five minutes
Draft immediately and skip checking

choice_rationales.A: This prevents drafting before purpose is clear.

parts.correct_explanation: The first sequence uses the planning window purposefully.

options.text: Recycling is a topic many people discuss.
Focus: a science fair-test method helped me compare two recycling signs before changing the whole system.
I will explain every science experiment.
Our school is perfect.

parts.correct_explanation: The focus connects school learning to the new context.

parts.prompt: Which body-one note supplies credible evidence?

options.text: Say the new sign was amazing.
Invent an exact percentage increase.
Describe placing two different signs at comparable bins and recording sorting errors for one week.
Discuss the history of plastic.

choice_rationales.D: This drifts from the personal action.

parts.hint: Use observable actions without invented precision.
parts.correct_explanation: The trial details support the learning claim.

parts.prompt: Which body-two note develops the result responsibly?

options.text: Explain that one sign produced fewer sorting mistakes in the observation week, so the team tested it at another bin before wider use.
Claim the sign solved recycling forever.
Change to an unrelated sports story.
Repeat the introduction.

choice_rationales.A: This shows bounded evidence and adaptation.

parts.hint: Move from result to cautious next action.
parts.correct_explanation: The result supports a measured extension.

options.text: Add a new experiment
Repeat every procedure
Apologise for uncertainty
Return to how testing one change before scaling altered the writer's decisions

parts.prompt: Which final audit question is most useful?

options.text: Did I use the longest words possible?
Does every paragraph advance the lesson–action–result chain without unsupported claims?
Did I include every idea I brainstormed?
Is every sentence the same length?

parts.correct_explanation: The plan is ready when it is complete, focused and supportable.
